decision: Implement the requested MVP as a self-contained TypeScript project under outputs/romanian-id-prefill.
reason: The workspace is empty and the requested result should be runnable and easy to hand off.

decision: Validate historical and current Romanian MRZ layouts before defining extraction rules.
reason: The referenced conversation is untrusted data and its assertion that all cards have three 30-character lines may be inaccurate.

decision: Use synthetic identities exclusively for automated and visual verification.
reason: Real identity images and OCR output must stay out of project artifacts and logs.

decision: Use React 19.3, Vite 8.3, TypeScript, Tesseract.js 7.0.0 and mrz 5.0.2 with parser autocorrect explicitly disabled.
reason: The OCR library documents browser WebWorkers/WASM and self-hosted assets; npm confirms releases on 2025-12-15 and 2026-03-11 respectively.

decision: Pin the BSD-3-Clause Doubango tesseractMRZ fast LSTM model at commit 1e7adfecda5f3c9ae1fb12cf6b4b8c3958c63e46 and vendor it locally with a checksum and license.
reason: It targets MRZ rather than general prose. The upstream model repository is archived (2021), so this is a frozen asset, not a maintained SDK; validate actual browser compatibility and synthetic OCR before handoff.

decision: Preload OCR before image selection, disable IndexedDB model caching, terminate the worker after each scan, and reset canvases and input references.
reason: Processing must make no network requests and images/OCR data must not be persisted. New scans prepare a fresh worker only after old image cleanup.

decision: Create a public GitHub repository named romanian-id-prefill on the authenticated alexcatdad account; target GitHub Pages with a manually triggered acceptance-gated deployment workflow.
reason: The user explicitly requested GitHub repository setup and Pages deployment after acceptance, and explicitly chose public visibility. Do not deploy the site until that acceptance arrives.

decision: Use the selected full-screen Local ID concept with local fonts and required crop/camera/validation/review states.
reason: A focused upload-to-review tool serves the MVP; the design reference is not deployment acceptance.

decision: Support verified Romanian TD2 (two 36-character rows) and TD1 (three 30-character rows). Reconstruct older CNP only from the documented optional SJJNNNC field plus DOB; read current TD1 CNP directly from line-one optional data.
reason: Official PRADO CI and government CEI specimens plus HG295/2021 verify these layouts; S is never inferred from sex/date.

decision: Accept the modern nationwide CNP code 70; conservatively require a known century for full CNP date validation and show ambiguity for S=7,8,9.
reason: MAI confirms code70. Foreign-resident sex codes do not determine a birth century, so a complete birth date cannot be asserted without extra evidence.

decision: Use bounded, signature-verified image decoding, full-width MRZ crop controls, and in-memory camera capture with tracks stopped on every exit.
reason: This makes the MVP usable without a heavyweight detector while keeping image and camera resources ephemeral. Perspective correction and HEIC/PDF are explicitly out of scope.

decision: Restrict the OCR worker to same-origin asset loading, lock fetch/XHR before its first image, and close failed initialization workers.
reason: Self-hosting alone does not prove an absence of processing-time requests; enforce the lifecycle and verify it with browser network tests.

decision: CIS TD1 cards may omit CNP from the MRZ. Preserve a checked MRZ/name candidate, leave CNP blank, and require manual CNP entry and validation.
reason: The official ROU-BO-06001 specimen has only fillers in optional data. Never infer a missing CNP.

decision: Accept historical CNP allocation codes 47/48 as a compatibility choice, without claiming current allocation authority.
reason: The requested CNP requirement is checksum/date validation; blanket rejection of older codes would exceed the evidence and unnecessarily block review.

decision: When country-field OCR fails, re-read its actual symbol-bounded pixels using the ICAO letter-only alphabet. Never enable parser substitutions or alter numeric/check-digit fields.
reason: Browser testing found O read as0 in ROU on clean synthetic images. A separately constrained local OCR read fixed the result while keeping invalid/uncertain reads blocked and disclosing the re-read in review.

decision: Validate manually edited CNP against MRZ DOB/sex as well as checksum/date, and reset acknowledgement on every edit.
reason: A syntactically valid CNP from a different person must not pass the confirmed-prefill gate, including on CIS cards that require manual entry.

decision: Encode the OCR canvas as an in-memory PNG data string before passing it to Tesseract; the library decodes it directly to bytes without a network request.
reason: Actual WebKit offline tests exposed a FileReader failure that left Tesseract's canvas-loading promise pending. Chromium and WebKit now pass the offline scan/review test.

decision: Reject multiple different complete MRZ blocks even when the second has a damaged country or sex field.
reason: A read-only peer review reproduced silent selection when a second issuer was read as IDR0U. Count plausible blocks before strict field validation and cover both formats with regressions.

decision: Close all unused worker transport entry points, guard XHR send and script loading, and await reader retirement before returning from page cache.
reason: Peer review found that fetch/XHR-open alone did not cover the worker's complete transport surface and that an interrupted startup could reuse a retiring promise. Also dispose idle workers after preprocessing failures; verify model retry and page-cache recovery in both browser engines.

decision: Show MRZ/CNP validation summaries and keep the complete original-reading check list in an accessible disclosure.
reason: Review should keep editable fields and confidence visible without a long list dominating the screen. Edited values have separate validation and always require fresh acknowledgement.

decision: Promise offline OCR/review after image decoding, without claiming universal offline file-selection compatibility.
reason: WebKit's automated offline mode refuses Blob/File reads. Both demo and uploaded TD2 crops can still run actual OCR offline; online decoding sends no HTTP request. This tested boundary is documented explicitly.

decision: Verify production UI against the 1536x1024 concept and at a 390x844 phone viewport; exercise actual local OCR and human acknowledgement in the retained in-app preview.
reason: The MVP must be reviewable before publication. The reference copy, composition, type scale, palette and icons were compared; functional additions and minor differences are recorded in docs/DESIGN.md.

decision: The exact GitHub Pages subpath production build passed 94 unit tests and 28 Chromium/WebKit browser checks; the root production preview was restored for review.
reason: Verification includes actual WASM OCR, offline demo and uploaded-crop reads, zero processing HTTP requests, blank storage, buffer/worker cleanup, camera capture/cancellation, MRZ/CNP mismatch rejection, model retry, and page-cache recovery. All test identities are synthetic; real-photo accuracy and hardware-camera acceptance remain to be established.

decision: Publish source to the requested public repository without dispatching Pages, and verify the exact pushed commit in GitHub CI.
reason: Commit 76ba964 passed the local production gates, then GitHub run36424847300 passed 94 unit and27 browser checks but exposed a Linux WebKit readiness timeout in the synthetic camera fixture. The fixture now paints live frames after captureStream starts, consistent with the canvas-capture specification; product camera readiness checks remain intact.

decision: Support both GitHub Pages subpath and Vercel root static hosting; keep website publication manual and pending explicit acceptance.
reason: The user explicitly requires either host. Vercel configuration carries equivalent restrictive headers and no runtime integrations; no project was connected or published.

decision: Set Safari 18+ on macOS and iOS/iPadOS 18+ as the primary compatibility baseline, with modern Chrome/Edge/Firefox support.
reason: Explicit browser build targets and Chromium/Firefox/desktop-mobile WebKit automation reduce regression risk. Shipping Safari and physical-camera acceptance require the documented hardware checklist; no certification is inferred.

decision: Support English and Romanian interface text, including validation/error/accessibility text, while preserving MRZ-only OCR.
reason: The user requested both languages. Romanian names may be restored with diacritics during required review; MRZ itself uses ICAO text.

decision: Run continuous browser verification in Chromium, Firefox, desktop WebKit and mobile WebKit, under both root and GitHub Pages base paths.
reason: Both deployment targets and Safari-first compatibility must remain reproducible. Include bilingual OCR/review and zero-network language switching; actual Safari hardware acceptance remains separately documented.

decision: Bundle English/Romanian copy and load every Latin and Latin-extended font face before enabling image selection.
reason: WebKit skipped some Unicode subsets when preloading by sample text, producing late font requests in review. Explicit FontFace.load for every bundled face passes zero-request English/Romanian switching tests. Language choice is in memory only and never transforms identity values.

decision: Publish the accepted MVP to GitHub Pages following the user’s explicit “do it” instruction.
result: Successful deployment; HTTPS enforced. Public-site Chromium and WebKit checks passed: local assets/CSP, synthetic offline OCR, bilingual mandatory review, zero processing requests, empty browser storage, and clear/reset. Physical Safari camera acceptance remains pending.

decision: Add PDF page selection using pinned Mozilla PDF.js 6.3.289 legacy build, with no PDF text extraction or hosted viewer.
reason: The user requested local PDF support. Rendering a selected page reuses the established crop/MRZ validation/review path and preserves Safari targeting.

decision: Preload PDF workers, standard fonts, CMaps and decoder resources before file selection; use a memory-only binary factory and block worker networking.
reason: Self-hosting alone is insufficient for the no-processing-network guarantee. Source PDFs are passed only as local bytes and are discarded when a page is selected or the operation ends.

decision: Bound PDFs to 15 MB, 50 pages, 2600-pixel render sides, 40MP embedded images and 45-second operations; reject password-required documents.
reason: These limits keep the browser MVP bounded and provide explicit recoverable failures rather than guessing or retaining a document.

decision: Gate page selection on the current rendered page and keep file inputs disabled while readers are being replaced.
reason: Browser regression tests caught brief stale-readiness windows during PDF page changes and discard cleanup. Workers and returned canvases have explicit ownership; cleanup is bounded and generation-guarded.

decision: Record the supplied ITL 054 template as the target for structured seller/buyer prefill in docs/CONTRACT_PARTY_FIELDS.md.
reason: User clarified the end goal. Inspection confirms 35 widgets per party, including addresses, contact and conditional representation fields. MRZ alone cannot provide these; current CEI domicile is not printed. This is a requirements record, not implementation or deployment acceptance.

decision: Implement ID understanding only: extend MRZ document fields and add local printed-field OCR with review for a single uploaded card side. Seller/buyer orchestration, contact/fiscal-address collection and contract generation belong to another project.
reason: The user explicitly narrowed the end goal to understanding the ID. Extract only evidence present in the image; do not infer an absent CEI address or silently merge identities.

decision: Use separate preloaded local ron+eng tessdata_fast OCR for labelled printed fields, alongside the unchanged restricted MRZ model.
reason: The contract-related identity fields include printed domicile and document details. Every candidate is reviewable; the generic title does not determine CI/CEI/CIS, and unavailable components remain blank. Models are pinned and hash checked; no source or OCR data leaves the browser.

decision: Support explicit printed-only reading without claiming MRZ validation, while MRZ-mode check failures continue blocking confirmation.
reason: Some card sides lack MRZ. Printed-only CNP still requires checksum/date validation. Conflicts between independent reads are displayed. This does not prove identity authenticity.

decision: Keep raw domicile text and structured components from contradicting each other after manual edits.
reason: Review found stale components/full text could otherwise be confirmed together. Editing either representation clears the other and resets review. A failed full-image copy also explicitly clears its canvas.

decision: Verify expanded ID understanding before publication; leave deployment awaiting acceptance.
result: 119 unit tests and 124 browser checks passed for root and Pages-subpath builds. Final review/address-edit changes additionally passed all 20 printed-ID browser checks at root and the full Pages suite. Desktop/phone visual checks showed no horizontal overflow or app runtime errors; WebKit screenshot injection caused only capture-time CSP warnings. Synthetic printed cards only; real-photo accuracy and physical Safari acceptance remain unbenchmarked.

decision: Replace MRZ jargon in the primary UI with visual code-row guidance in English and Romanian.
reason: The user noted that people using the app will not know MRZ. Show an example, ask a visual yes/no question, use Read my ID, and retain technical validation details in a disclosure without weakening checks.

decision: Extract installable ESM TypeScript library with framework-independent core, optional React 19 review UI and same-origin runtime asset copy CLI. Demo consumes public package exports. Verify actual packed installation; deliver local archive without registry publication or site deployment.
reason: Reuse ID understanding in a future contract app while preserving explicit review and browser-local processing.

decision: Library v0.2.0 verified: 142 unit tests; 124 browser cases each at root and Pages subpath; isolated tarball installation verifies React-free core, typed React consumer, same-origin asset copying and offline OCR/PDF in Chromium/WebKit. Deliver local archive; no npm registry publication or site deployment.
limitations: Synthetic fixtures establish regression behavior, not physical Safari camera or real-photo accuracy. Host owns confirmed callback data.

decision: Split into independently versioned npm workspaces @alexcatdad/browser-ocr (generic OCR/image/PDF runtime) and @alexcatdad/roid (Romanian ID parsing, validation, orchestration and optional React review). Root becomes private demo; one-way ROID dependency on OCR.
reason: User wants OCR development independent of Romanian ID and future contract features. OCR returns caller-owned text/geometry/confidence; ROID interprets/discards raw text and preserves review constraints.
distribution: Local archives until registry publication is separately requested; keep current repository.

decision: Verified separate OCR/ROID packages before handoff.
validation: 149 unit tests (21 OCR, 128 ROID); 124 demo browser tests at each root and Pages paths; independent packed installs and strict browser TypeScript; Chromium/WebKit generic repeated OCR, ROID review callback and PDF rendering with zero processing requests.
result: OCR public types hide engine/Node types; composed asset CLI normalizes package paths and preserves host files. Two local archives; source only, no registry publication or website deployment.

decision: Move OCR to public alexcatdad/browser-ocr repository, extracting its package history. ROID remains here and consumes an exact external Git commit with npm preparation; no sibling-directory dependency or bundled source copy.
reason: User requested a separate OCR repository for independent development.
distribution: Repository source publication authorized; npm registry publication and website deployment remain separate.

decision: Adopt independently verified OCR commit 1501c83fc27d100068370216055061ceea540d90 from alexcatdad/browser-ocr; remove OCR workspace/source/models and use its installed public API/assets.
validation: OCR repo: 22 units and independent Chromium/WebKit packed consumer pass; GitHub CI green. ROID: 130 units, 124 root plus 124 Pages browser checks, and fresh-cache ROID-only archive installation with SSH disabled resolves exact external Git pin; consumer OCR/PDF/review/privacy checks pass in Chromium/WebKit.
result: ROID version0.3.1 depends on OCR0.1.1 immutable Git commit; package-specific engine tests remain in OCR, adapter tests mock public OCR API. No registry publication or site deployment.
